title: Atomic multi-target damage-skill resolution with per-target facts
objective: Generalize the already-verified negative absolute HP damage-skill mechanic to enemy-all/row/column target sets while spending MP once and preserving target identity in resolved facts.
hypothesis: If selection completes and every semantic/resource precondition is validated before mutation, one cast can spend MP once, mutate several target states deterministically, and expose one target-associated Damage fact per affected actor without changing the existing single-target ABI.
claim_boundary: No original PAL3 damage formula is claimed. This experiment reuses the existing deterministic absolute-HP effect only; healing, statuses, ally damage, ElementPosition geometry, Unity presentation/runtime and VFX remain outside scope.
design_constraints: Keep CombatEvent and SkillCastResolution ABI unchanged.
Use additive MultiTargetSkillCastResolution<TKey> and TargetSkillResolution<TKey> types.
Spend MP once per cast, never once per target.
Reject invalid semantics, empty target sets, insufficient MP and damage overflow before any target mutation.
Reject aliased combatant-state instances before mutation, including caster-as-enemy-target aliasing.
Delegate target discovery/order to verified CombatTargetResolver<TKey>.
Preserve one overall SkillCast fact and target-associated Damage/TargetDefeated facts.

attempts.description: Add an enemy all/row/column multi-target resolver and atomicity/event tests without modifying the verified single-target resolver or presentation planner.
attempts.fix: Pre-CI contract review added state-instance alias guards after identifying that unique keys alone would still allow two target keys to reference one CombatantState, or allow caster state to appear as an enemy target. Two regression tests were added before machine execution.

next_recommended_experiment: If verified, decide whether Step 5C should add a multi-target presentation planner or proceed to Step 6 healing/support while keeping presentation downstream.
